findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference is ignored.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, eight 2-second animations remained running; CSS inspection found no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential animation and autoplay behavior in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and provide a reduced/static state.

findings.summary: High-contrast users receive low-contrast text and no contrast-specific adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling. Lighthouse measured ratios as low as 1.75:1 on the age banner and 3.29:1 on view counts.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast styles, preserve system colors, and raise text/UI contrast to WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Route changes have no continuity transition.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS contained no view-transition declarations and representative routes are full-document navigations with abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions for route continuity, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Sticky chrome does not adapt as content scrolls.
findings.evidence: At scrollY 1200 the 84px age-verification bar remained sticky at top; CSS had no scroll-state query or scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse or soften persistent chrome after scrolling using scroll-state-aware styling while keeping verification accessible.

findings.summary: Menus and transient controls do not use resilient anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The page exposes multiple header/dropdown controls, while CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and fallback position-try rules for menus and tooltips near viewport edges.

findings.summary: The consent modal and menu overlays are custom rather than semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The visible modal blocks the page, but DOM inspection found 0 dialog, 0 popover, and 0 details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with dialog and transient menus with popover, including declarative light-dismiss and focus restoration.

findings.summary: Dense chrome and promotions crowd the primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show two navigation rows, a persistent verification banner, a 190px sidebar, consent UI, and promotional cards surrounding the video grid/player.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent navigation and promotional chrome, prioritize the media grid/player, and progressively disclose secondary categories.

findings.summary: The mobile layout renders a 1024px desktop canvas inside a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout measurements on both home and video pages reported scrollWidth 1024, visual viewport 360, and 664px horizontal overflow. The mobile screenshot shows clipped navigation and cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 1024px minimum layout, honor the device viewport, and use fluid grids/intrinsic sizing that reflow at 360px without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Reused content components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules, while the same sidebar/card layout remains desktop-sized and clipped in the 360px condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable regions containment and apply size-aware container queries to cards, navigation, and sidebars.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and some touch targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing the first visible link produced outline-style none and no box shadow. Lighthouse also found 20px-high targets and insufficient spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment and ensure interactive targets provide at least 24px safe space, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Mobile largest-contentful paint misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.9s and FCP 3.0s (performance 0.83); the separate trace measured LCP 1.98s, showing condition-sensitive performance.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, cut startup script/CSS cost, and validate LCP below 2.5s on representative mobile hardware.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript creates blocking main-thread work.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 2 long tasks, a longest task of 188.28ms, and 151.79ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks into scheduled chunks and defer non-critical feed, consent, and promotional code.

findings.summary: The startup dependency graph is request-heavy and delays rendering.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 144 requests, 62 scripts, 11 stylesheets, 1.77MB transferred, and multiple parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse LCP was 3.9s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce startup dependencies, inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, and tune preload/fetch priority around the LCP asset.

findings.summary: Substantial unused CSS and JavaScript ship on mobile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 26,972 wasted JS bytes in assetsLoader and 94.9%/89.7% waste in two mobile stylesheets; HAR recorded 62 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by page capability, remove unused selectors, and load optional feed/player modules only when needed.

findings.summary: Some interactive controls lack or mismatch accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name and label-content-name-mismatch, including an unnamed filter button and video links whose accessible name omits visible duration text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name that includes its visible label and preserve native element semantics.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 1.75:1 age-banner secondary text, 2.15:1 banner primary text, and 3.29:1 view counts against their backgrounds.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the green banner and muted-text color tokens to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text/UI.

findings.summary: Focus and list semantics do not provide a reliable keyboard/AT structure.
findings.evidence: The focused GB link had no visible outline. Lighthouse found a ul with direct div, complementary, and role=button children instead of li elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible :focus-visible styling, keep list children semantic, and ensure focus order follows the visual card order.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow is restricted and mobile content does not reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no in the effective mobile viewport and undersized targets; 360px layout evidence recorded 664px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no, support at least 400% zoom/reflow, eliminate fixed-width overflow, and enlarge crowded targets.

findings.summary: Image markup does not reserve or consistently right-size media.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29 of 36 images missing dimensions and 12 oversized relative to display size, despite valid doctype/charset and correct sampled aspect ratios.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio on every thumbnail and serve a closer responsive candidate for each rendered card size.

findings.summary: Localized indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The page had a canonical URL and robots.txt allowed core pages, but exposed no hreflang links across its many language hosts; /sitemap.xml returned 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish reciprocal hreflang links for localized equivalents and expose a valid sitemap location in robots.txt.

findings.summary: Video pages omit structured entity data.
findings.evidence: The representative detail page had useful Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD VideoObject; og:image:type declared image/jpeg for a .webp URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD and make Open Graph media MIME declarations match the served asset.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protection are incomplete.
findings.evidence: CSP is only frame-ancestors self, offering no script/style XSS policy. The settings and x_csrf_token cookies were not Secure; settings also used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP beyond frame-ancestors and set Secure plus an appropriate SameSite value on every HTTPS cookie.

findings.summary: The initial page makes a very broad cross-origin request set.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 117 of 144 requests and 1.66MB of 1.77MB to non-main origins; tracker enumeration found 14 third-party origins, including Google, tsydndicate and collector endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat owned CDNs separately but minimize external vendors, gate optional analytics/ads on consent, and batch collection with short retention.

findings.summary: Authentication offers federated/email methods but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load, but the sign-up surface offered Google, X and email/password only; no passkey text or WebAuthn flow was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication alongside existing methods, requested only after explicit user action.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent or too narrow.
findings.evidence: Headers lacked X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy. Permissions-Policy only set two client-hint directives and the CSP had no broader XSS controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a restrictive Referrer-Policy, an allowlist Permissions-Policy, and strengthen CSP/Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: Localized markup relies heavily on physical CSS directions.
findings.evidence: html lang was correctly nl, but inspected CSS contained about 695 physical left/right declarations versus 26 logical inline/block declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout spacing/positioning to logical properties and verify representative RTL locales with dir=rtl.

findings.summary: Abbreviated counts are not formatted for the Dutch locale.
findings.evidence: The Dutch page renders values such as 8.7M and 600.5K; Dutch formatting convention uses comma decimals and locale-aware compact notation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Intl.NumberFormat with the active locale and compact notation rather than hand-built K/M strings.

findings.summary: Sign-up errors are visible but not programmatically announced.
findings.evidence: Empty submission displayed Dutch required/password messages, but inputs had no aria-invalid and no role=alert/live-region messages were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Synchronize visible validation with aria-invalid, associate messages using aria-describedby, and announce the error summary after submit.

findings.summary: The sign-up email field disables useful autofill.
findings.evidence: The email input used autocomplete=off while the password correctly used new-password; required semantics were not exposed on either field.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email and new-password, native required attributes, and stable input names so password managers and autofill can assist.

findings.summary: Thumbnail delivery wastes image bytes and omits layout reservations.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 12 oversized images, 29 missing dimensions, 8 below-fold images not lazy, and 16 legacy-format detections.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve closer srcset candidates, lazy-load below-fold media, reserve dimensions, and prefer modern formats throughout.

findings.summary: Startup does disproportionate script work for a content listing.
findings.evidence: The page loaded 62 scripts totaling about 1.01MB and the trace recorded 151.79ms blocking time, while Lighthouse identified large unused CSS/JS portions.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer background/promotion modules, conditionally load page-specific features, and remove unused mobile bundles.

findings.summary: Cross-origin scripts and media dominate the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: Non-main origins accounted for 1.66MB and 117 requests; scripts alone transferred 1.01MB before a video was played.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer ads/social identity until interaction or consent, and cache/conditionally load heavy media integrations.

findings.summary: The initial heap footprint is large for a listing before playback.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 678,439 nodes and 36.1MB self size; after repeated scrolling it reached 743,136 nodes and 39.3MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile feed/card allocations, virtualize or release offscreen items, and conditionally initialize promotional/player modules.
